## Failure Modes

Contract drift, misplaced caller authority, unbounded inputs, duplicate effects, misleading completion, and unsafe error or diagnostic disclosure.

## Checklist

Complete applicable items only with evidence. Record unresolved choices and the reason for any skipped or inapplicable item.

- [ ] The owned API contract agrees with changed operations, inputs, results, and public errors.
- [ ] Affected caller, resource, and tenant permissions are enforced at the responsible effect boundary, including relevant denial paths.
- [ ] Input limits, pagination, and compatibility behavior are defined where affected without exposing unbounded work or silently changing consumer assumptions.
- [ ] Retry-prone or concurrent mutations define effect identity, conflicting reuse, completion, and reconciliation for unknown outcomes.
- [ ] Public errors and diagnostics preserve useful causes and actual effect state while protecting secrets and private payloads.
- [ ] Affected consumers and relevant accepted, rejected, interrupted, or recovery paths have evidence or explicit verification gaps.

## Validation

- Relevant validation names: contract, test, smoke, check
- Select configured checks from VALIDATION.md for the affected contracts and failure paths.
- Report skipped or unconfigured checks with reasons and remaining risk; they are not passing evidence.

## Failure Modes

Incompatible readers or writers, lost user changes, competing migrations, incomplete backfills, irreversible data effects, and unverified cutover.

## Checklist

Complete applicable items only with evidence. Record unresolved choices and the reason for any skipped or inapplicable item.

- [ ] Schema and data authority, before-and-after invariants, and the state that must survive the migration are identified.
- [ ] Affected readers and writers have a compatible transition and cutover sequence, including old/new version overlap where required.
- [ ] Concurrent execution, lock or capacity limits, checkpoints, and resumable backfills are defined where affected.
- [ ] Recovery distinguishes reversible changes, forward repair, and reconciliation; incomplete recovery preserves original causes and remaining paths.
- [ ] Before-and-after data checks establish relevant constraints and consumer-visible correctness rather than only command completion.
- [ ] Cutover and cleanup status are supported by evidence, and remaining deployment, backfill, or recovery work is explicit.

## Validation

- Relevant validation names: migration-check, test, smoke, check
- Select configured checks from VALIDATION.md for the affected contracts and failure paths.

- [ ] Replacement, removal, or recovery accounts for affected data and interfaces rather than assuming a version change can reverse every effect.

## Failure Modes

Declared and active state diverge, uncertain external effects are repeated, recovery is incompatible with data, critical journeys remain broken, and completion is overstated.

## Checklist

Complete applicable items only with evidence. Record unresolved choices and the reason for any skipped or inapplicable item.

- [ ] Affected user journeys, operating owners, declared configuration, and observed active state are identified.
- [ ] The authorized change, compatibility constraints, stop conditions, and partial states are understood before external effects are applied or repeated.
- [ ] Rollback, reconciliation, or forward repair matches the effects that can actually be reversed and preserves valid user state.
- [ ] Relevant configuration, credentials, telemetry, and restore prerequisites have owners and evidence appropriate to the changed behavior.
- [ ] Critical journeys and intended active behavior are verified; artifact delivery or a healthy process alone is distinguished from successful operation.
- [ ] Original and recovery failures, mixed or unknown state, and remaining activation or handoff work are reported accurately.

## Failure Modes

Unrepresentative measurements, changed workloads mistaken for improvements, resource pressure, unbounded work, stale cache results, and hidden correctness tradeoffs.

## Checklist

Complete applicable items only with evidence. Record unresolved choices and the reason for any skipped or inapplicable item.

- [ ] The affected journey or hot path, representative workload, supported environment, and relevant resource limits are identified.
- [ ] Measurements name artifact and environment identity, observation points, units, comparable baseline, and meaningful uncertainty or regression thresholds.
- [ ] Relevant latency, memory, payload, I/O, or queue evidence covers operating conditions and tails rather than only a favorable average.
- [ ] Changed concurrency, allocation, caching, or batching preserves agreed correctness, freshness, identity, and lifecycle behavior.
- [ ] Overload, deadlines, cancellation, and bounded admission or recovery are accounted for where work can outlive its usefulness.
- [ ] Observed results and tradeoffs support the stated improvement, with unmeasured environments and remaining verification gaps explicit.

## Failure Modes

Wrong trust or effect authority, alternate-path access, identity leakage, unsafe input interpretation, excessive capabilities, and sensitive data exposure.

## Checklist

Complete applicable items only with evidence. Record unresolved choices and the reason for any skipped or inapplicable item.

- [ ] Affected assets, trust crossings, caller capabilities, and protected effects are identified from the actual system boundary.
- [ ] Relevant resource, account, and tenant authority is enforced on every reachable protected path, including rejected or revoked access.
- [ ] Untrusted input is validated and interpreted as data at the responsible boundary; alternate entrypoints and unsafe output contexts are accounted for.
- [ ] Credentials and private data have appropriate access, redaction, retention, and deletion boundaries across logs, examples, caches, and artifacts.
- [ ] External integrations and capabilities stay within the agreed authority, with failure, revocation, and uncertain effects handled where affected.
- [ ] Evidence covers relevant accepted and rejected cases and the actual exposure path; unverified conditions and remaining risks are explicit.

## Validation

- Relevant validation names: lint, test, smoke, check
- Select configured checks from VALIDATION.md for the affected contracts and failure paths.

## Task Skills

Choose the applicable skill by its stated purpose and read its contract sources before editing. This list reflects the skills generated for the selected scope, repository type, addons, and density; it does not grant command or delivery authority. Update the list when the project retires or replaces a skill.

- [feature](skills/feature/SKILL.md): Implement new or expanded product behavior from project requirements, ownership boundaries, and observable acceptance criteria.
- [bugfix](skills/bugfix/SKILL.md): Diagnose and repair observed incorrect behavior using a reproducible trigger, the intended contract, and evidence of actual effects and recovery.
- [refactor](skills/refactor/SKILL.md): Reorganize implementation responsibilities while preserving agreed observable behavior, ownership, and consumer contracts.
- [ops-change](skills/ops-change/SKILL.md): Change operating configuration, rollout, or recovery behavior with evidence of active state, affected journeys, and reversible or irreversible effects.
- [dependency-upgrade](skills/dependency-upgrade/SKILL.md): Select, update, or remove a dependency based on necessity, supported compatibility, reproducible evidence, and replacement or recovery cost.
- [test-hardening](skills/test-hardening/SKILL.md): Improve evidence for existing behavior or a demonstrated regression through independent expectations, meaningful failure fixtures, and proportionate execution cost.
- [backend-api](skills/backend-api/SKILL.md): Change backend request and response behavior, caller permissions, or effect completion while keeping the owned API contract and consumers consistent.
- [db-migration](skills/db-migration/SKILL.md): Change persistent schemas or data through a compatible transition with explicit invariants, reader and writer coordination, and recovery evidence.

## Work Guidance

- Identify the contract, invariant, or user-visible risk whose current evidence is weak. Determine what observation would disprove correctness rather than starting from an arbitrary coverage target.
- Define the expected result independently of the implementation. Include relevant rejection, interruption, partial-effect, or recovery states rather than checking only a successful call.
- Control ordering or failures where needed and report unsupported conditions as explicit gaps. Avoid timing repetition, swallowed fixture errors, and assertions that would pass after removing the protected behavior.
- Run the narrow checks that establish the risk. Remove redundant or obsolete checks only after confirming that their required evidence remains covered.

## Validation Scope

- Relevant validation names: contract, test, smoke, check
- Stable names and executable routing come from root VALIDATION.md and the configured runner. Do not infer commands from this guide.
- Select checks for affected contracts and failure paths. Review-only changes may use focused document or contract review; scaffold text does not prove implemented runtime behavior.

## Required Evidence

- Compare affected operations, request and response shapes, public errors, and limits with the owned contract and representative consumer expectations.
- For affected access boundaries, observe accepted and rejected callers, resource or tenant isolation, and invalid or excessive inputs at the responsible operation.
- For retry-prone effects, verify duplicate and conflicting requests, interruption, and unknown-outcome reconciliation against actual state where implemented.
- Check affected consumers and diagnostics for compatibility, useful failure causes, accurate completion, and exclusion of private values; record untested combinations.

## Report

Record the affected contract, artifact and environment where relevant, executed checks, actual results, skipped checks and reasons, and remaining work or risk.
Distinguish planned, delivered, active, and completed state where relevant. This guide does not authorize deployment or additional external effects.

## Repository Scope

Scope: backend

This repository owns API server behavior, server-side domain rules, authentication,
authorization, persistence, migrations, observability, and backend security.

This repository does not own frontend routing, visual design, component hierarchy,
design tokens, or browser interaction policy.

Frontend-facing behavior is contracted through `api/openapi.yaml`, `api/examples/*.json`, `docs/backend/04-http-api-policy.md`, and `docs/backend/05-error-response.md`.



## Source of Truth

- Product scope: docs/product/02-spec.md
- Architecture decisions: docs/adr/*.md
- Validation: VALIDATION.md
- Agent routing: .agents/context-map.md
- Repository hygiene: .editorconfig, .gitattributes, .gitignore

## Hard Rules

- Do not generate or infer application source code from this scaffold.
- Do not invent technology choices. Use UNDECIDED when a decision is not known.
- Do not create fake credentials, tokens, secrets, or private values.
- Do not rely on generated, cache, or build output as source truth.

## Repository Hygiene

- .editorconfig sets line ending, encoding, and final newline policy.
- .gitattributes sets Git text normalization and binary diff policy.
- .gitignore excludes local, secret, build, and cache artifacts.
- Generated, cache, and build output must not be used as design-document evidence.
- Do not create large diffs that only change line endings.

## Before Editing

- Read this file, VALIDATION.md, CHECKLIST.md, and .agents/context-map.md.
- Read the skill and checklist named by the context map.
- Confirm source-of-truth documents before changing contracts.

## Out of Scope

- Application source scaffolding.
- Runtime infrastructure such as Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or framework apps.
- Project-specific credentials or deployment secrets.

## Final Response Requirements

- List executed validations, passed validations, skipped validations, skip reasons, and remaining risk.
- Name any source-of-truth documents changed.
- Call out API, DB, repository hygiene, and runner changes explicitly.

- Local UI State: temporary visual or interaction state owned by one component area.
- Global Client State: client-owned state allowed only by explicit allowlist.

- Observe affected journeys and loading, empty, disabled, failure, and retry states, checking that recoverable input and appropriate feedback remain usable.
- Compare actual requests and responses with the selected API contract, including changed rejection, delayed-response, and uncertain-effect handling.
- Where asynchronous or persisted state changes, verify that obsolete results and previous account or tenant state cannot replace current intent or leak into another session.
- Inspect affected controls, labels, keyboard operation, focus, and dynamic status in the rendered interface; report assistive-technology and environment gaps separately from automated checks.

## Report

Record the affected contract, artifact and environment where relevant, executed checks, actual results, skipped checks and reasons, and remaining work or risk.
Distinguish planned, delivered, active, and completed state where relevant. This guide does not authorize deployment or additional external effects.

- Global Client State: client-owned state allowed only by explicit allowlist.

## Maintaining a View

- Replace UNDECIDED identities, boundaries, edge actions, and branch conditions with evidence from the decision source. Remove branches that do not apply.
- Keep composition views separate from operation flows. Data-model edges do not assert cardinality until the project specifies it.
- Label all interactions and outcomes. For operation flows, record failure, interruption, partial state, recovery ownership, and bounded retry rules where reachable.
- Keep reported success consistent with observable completion; a cancellation or timeout does not by itself prove that external effects were undone.
- Update the source document and related decision record when meaning changes, then update the diagram. Preserve project-specific edits during scaffold updates.
- Review rendered Mermaid output in the project's chosen viewer; source generation alone does not verify layout or accessibility. Keep the reader question and decision source available as a text description.

## Work Guidance

- Identify the supported platforms and versions, lifecycle owners, permission or capability contract, and affected user journeys. Follow existing platform choices and distinguish documentation assumptions from device behavior.
- Define what survives suspension, process loss, interruption, or offline use. Assign ownership of queued effects and synchronization conflicts, and reconcile uncertain completion before retrying external mutations.
- Preserve recoverable user work while isolating account and tenant data. Account for sign-out, identity switches, permission revocation, and deletion across local state, queued work, and remote copies.
- Verify relevant supported journeys and interruption or recovery behavior with suitable platform evidence. Keep untested platforms, store delivery, and incomplete synchronization explicit.

## Validation Scope

Verify supported device journeys and lifecycle transitions with evidence of preserved user work and actual recovery.

## Validation Selection

- Relevant validation names: test, smoke, docs, check
- Stable names and executable routing come from root VALIDATION.md and the configured runner. Do not infer commands from this guide.
- Select checks for affected contracts and failure paths. Review-only changes may use focused document or contract review; scaffold text does not prove implemented runtime behavior.
- Unconfigured or skipped checks require reasons and remaining risk; they are not passing evidence.

## Required Evidence

- Exercise affected foreground, suspension, process-loss, and offline transitions on the supported platforms, observing pending work and recoverable local state.
- Where synchronization or external effects change, verify conflicts, duplicate replay, interrupted operations, and reconciliation before uncertain work is repeated.
- For affected identity or capability boundaries, observe sign-out, account switching, denied or revoked permissions, and deletion across local, queued, and remote state.
- Verify affected app and data-version transitions and their recovery limits; distinguish device or installed-app evidence from compilation and untested platform claims.

## Report

Record the affected contract, artifact and environment where relevant, executed checks, actual results, skipped checks and reasons, and remaining work or risk.
Distinguish planned, delivered, active, and completed state where relevant. This guide does not authorize deployment or additional external effects.

## Work Guidance

- Review intended resource effects and compatibility with dependent services. Identify concurrent operators and state writers, and stay within the task's execution authority before applying or repeating changes.
- Prepare for partial application, interruption, drift, and unknown external outcomes. Use operation identity and observed state to choose rollback, reconciliation, or forward repair without assuming destructive effects can be undone.
- Verify the intended active state and critical dependent behavior. Report mixed or unknown state, remaining recovery work, and delivery gaps rather than treating a successful plan or apply command as complete service evidence.

## Validation and Delivery

Use repository rules and the task routes in VALIDATION.md to select relevant configured checks. Repair missing setup within the authorized scope or report the gap; an unconfigured or skipped check is not passing evidence.

Report observable changes, actual checks and results, remaining gaps, and incomplete recovery or delivery work. Follow existing execution and delivery authority; this skill does not authorize additional publication or external mutations.

## Work Guidance

- Identify input and output owners, dataset grain, schema or version identity, lineage, and consumer acceptance. Separate illustrative contracts from observed source data and published results.
- Define publication quality and freshness requirements and what happens to invalid, missing, duplicate, or late data. Keep quarantine or rejected results distinguishable from data that consumers may rely on.
- Assign identities and progress boundaries for replay, backfill, and concurrent work. Preserve valid existing changes, reconcile partial publication, and account for retention or deletion across derived copies and replay sources.
- Verify relevant data invariants and downstream behavior across success, restart, and reconciliation paths. A completed job alone does not prove correct lineage, complete publication, or removal of retained data.

## Validation and Delivery

Use repository rules and the task routes in VALIDATION.md to select relevant configured checks. Repair missing setup within the authorized scope or report the gap; an unconfigured or skipped check is not passing evidence.

Report observable changes, actual checks and results, remaining gaps, and incomplete recovery or delivery work. Follow existing execution and delivery authority; this skill does not authorize additional publication or external mutations.

- .editorconfig sets line ending, encoding, and final newline policy.
- .gitattributes sets Git text normalization and binary diff policy.
- .gitignore excludes local, secret, build, and cache artifacts.
- Generated, cache, and build output must not be used as design-document evidence.
- Do not create large diffs that only change line endings.

## Before Editing

- Read this file, VALIDATION.md, CHECKLIST.md, and .agents/context-map.md.
- Read the skill and checklist named by the context map.
- Confirm source-of-truth documents before changing contracts.

## Out of Scope

- Application source scaffolding.
- Runtime infrastructure such as Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, or framework apps.
- Project-specific credentials or deployment secrets.

## Final Response Requirements

- List executed validations, passed validations, skipped validations, skip reasons, and remaining risk.
- Name any source-of-truth documents changed.
- Call out API, DB, repository hygiene, and runner changes explicitly.
